title: ADR: synchronized-change-lifecycle-and-safety-gates-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide synchronized change lifecycle and a common set of safety gates that must be satisfied before any cross-cutting change is promoted from development to production. The goal is to reduce regressions, prevent silent data/contract drift, and make multi-service rollouts (API, infra, runtime, model-serving) observable and reversible.

Scope

- Applies to any change that touches two or more of the following domains: API surface, model artifacts, serving runtime binaries, infra/networking configuration, or telemetry/observability pipelines.
- Excludes isolated patch fixes limited to a single service with no public contract impact (see Exceptions section).

Motivation

Redwood runs a complex stack where model, runtime, and infra changes interact. We have observed incidents that originated from partial rollouts where one side of the change (for example, model inputs) was updated without coordinated validation on the runtime or observability side. This ADR creates a repeatable process and machine-checkable gates to reduce these risks while preserving deployment velocity.

Principles

1) Small, verifiable increments: prefer multiple small synchronized commits and feature flags rather than large monolithic changes.
2) Observable safety: every rollout must include automated checks that exercise both correctness and cost/latency regressions.
3) Rule-based rollback: rollbacks must be triggered by objective thresholds, not ad-hoc judgements.
4) Clear ownership: every cross-cutting rollout names a primary owner and an on-call fallback.

Safety Gates (machine-checkable)

Each synchronized change must pass the following gates before a production promotion:

1) Contract Compatibility Gate
- API schema compatibility test passes (no breaking changes unless approved in RFC).
- Output schema adapter tests (JSON/YAML examples) pass against a contract test harness.

2) Unit & Integration Gate
- Unit tests: 100% of modified modules pass.
- Integration tests: end-to-end smoke that validates request → runtime → model → response path: 
  - For model changes: validate inference outputs on a small deterministic prompt set (goldens).
  - For runtime changes: validate KV cache behavior and sequence-length routing on 3 synthetic workloads.

3) Performance & Cost Gate
- Latency: p95 across synthetic representative traffic must not exceed baseline p95 + 15% or absolute 250ms (whichever is lower) for low-latency tier routes.
- Throughput: for batch modes, throughput must not regress by more than 12% in the controlled testbed.
- Cost estimate: automated cost estimator must provide per-token delta and total projected monthly impact; must be below threshold for the owning team or have approved cost-exemption.

4) Observability Gate
- Instrumentation: all new code paths emit typed telemetry fields (trace_id, request_tag, model_variant, quantization_profile).
- Traceable path: end-to-end traces correlate across service hops and contain the rollout tag.
- Alerting: necessary SLI-derived alerts created in the monitoring workspace (owner's dashboard).

5) Compliance & Security Gate
- Secrets/KMS: no plaintext secrets in artifacts; KMS policies validated for private deployments.
- Data residency: for customer-sensitive datasets, change must include retention mapping and audit log tests.

6) Canary & Progressive Rollout Gate
- Canary window: validate canaries for a minimum of 2 business hours or 5K requests (whichever comes first) against live traffic channels using canary scoring metrics described below.
- Traffic ramp: automated ramp policy that increases traffic in steps (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with metric checks at each step.

Canary Scoring and Rollback Triggers

Canary validation uses an objective score synthesized from metrics in three categories: correctness, latency/cost, and error signals. Each category produces a normalized score (0–100), weighted as follows: correctness 0.50, latency/cost 0.30, errors 0.20. A canary passes if the weighted score >= 92.

Rollback is automatically triggered if any of the following occur during a ramp or steady-state observation window:
- Correctness score drops below 85
- p95 latency increases by >20% over baseline for the route
- Increase in 5xx rate by absolute 0.3 percentage points or relative >4x
- Any new privacy/audit failure reported by the compliance harness

Ownership and Roles

- Primary Owner: the authoring team is the primary owner of the rollout and is responsible for preflight checks and canary monitoring.
- Runtime Steward: eng-serving-runtime team ensures runtime compatibility and provides rollback patches.
- Observability Steward: eng-platform configures dashboards, alerting, and synthetic traffic.
- On-call Escalation: named project on-call rotates for the change window.

Change Lifecycle Procedure (numbered)

1) Preflight (local + CI)
   a) Create a rollout ticket using the change template and link PRs across repos.
   b) Run contract tests and integration smoke in CI (must be green).
   c) Run automated cost estimator and attach cost delta to ticket.
   d) Declare primary owner and runtime/observability stewards on the ticket.

2) Staging Verification
   a) Deploy to staging with the canary tag and run deterministic golden prompts (for models) and synthetic latency/throughput tests (for runtime/infra).
   b) Run the observability validation script to assert telemetry presence and trace correlation.

3) Canary in Production
   a) Programmatically create a canary release with an automated ramp policy.
   b) Monitor canary score dashboard and logs for the minimum window.
   c) If gates pass, progress ramp steps; otherwise trigger automatic rollback and page owners.

4) Post-Deployment Validation
   a) After 24 hours at full traffic, run a regression job against the production prompt-set and check for semantic drift items.
   b) Run cost reconciliation and publish the realized cost delta to the rollout ticket.

5) Bake and Close
   a) After 7 days without regression signals, mark the rollout as baked.
   b) Capture learnings and update the team-runbook with any corrective steps or dashboard improvements.

Exceptions and Fast-tracks

- Emergency Fixes: for outages or safety issues, owners may perform an expedited rollout with a post-hoc audit; the ticket must be created within 24 hours and include the retrospective.
- Low-risk UI-only changes restricted to a single web service may be fast-tracked if the owning PM and two engineers sign-off.

Tooling and Automation Requirements

The following tools/harnesses are required to implement these gates in CI/CD:
- Contract test harness (service-contract-oracle) integrated into PR pipelines.
- Canary orchestrator that supports incremental traffic ramping and scoring (we recommend extending the existing rollout service).
- Automated cost estimator that consumes simulated token distributions and returns per-route cost delta.
- Observability validation CLI that asserts telemetry fields and trace correlation.

Example checklist (to be attached to every cross-cutting rollout ticket)

- [ ] Rollout ticket created and linked PRs attached
- [ ] Contract compatibility tests green
- [ ] Integration smoke green
- [ ] Cost estimate attached and reviewed
- [ ] Observability validation passed in staging
- [ ] Canary created with ramp policy
- [ ] Alerts/dashboards in place for this rollout
- [ ] Post-deploy regression job scheduled

Non-goals

- This ADR does not mandate a particular canary duration for all services; local teams can adjust within the minimums stated.
- It does not replace per-service SLO setting and ownership; it complements them.

Open questions and future work

1) Automated semantic regression detection: integrate model-eval signals into the canary score (planned Q4 2026).
2) Cross-team rehearsals: periodic coordinated drills to validate the rollup pipeline under realistic load (game-days).

Compatibility with existing standards

- Aligns with the existing staged migration ADR and complements runtime-flag hot-reload guidelines. This ADR adds the synchronized lifecycle and unified scoring mechanism absent from those documents.

Appendix: Gate Criteria Table

| Gate Category | Required Artifacts | Minimum Threshold | Owner |
|--------------|-------------------|-------------------:|-------|
| Contract Compatibility | Contract test report, sample payloads | No breaking failures | Primary Owner |
| Unit & Integration | CI summaries, smoke logs | All tests passing | Primary Owner |
| Performance & Cost | Synthetic load report, cost delta | p95 <= baseline+15% cost delta approved | Runtime Steward |
| Observability | Validation report, dashboard links | Trace + typed telemetry present | Observability Steward |
| Security & Compliance | KMS audit, privacy test | No new failures | Security Team |

Related documents

- See the service-starter-kit safe-config patterns guide for templates used in preflight tickets.
- See the contract-oracle and canary orchestrator documentation for implementation details.
